assumptions: Analyze is_palindrome only, not the other functions or module-level benchmark. String indexing and character equality are O(1); input is excluded.
rationale: Time: The two indices move inward, comparing at most floor(n/2) character pairs. In the worst case all pairs are examined, so time is O(n). Auxiliary space: Only two integer indices are stored; no substring or reversed copy is created. Owner review: The selected is_palindrome function moves two indices inward and compares at most floor(n/2) character pairs, so worst-case time is O(n). It stores only the two indices, giving O(1) auxiliary space. The recursive and slicing helpers in the same file are outside this reviewed entrypoint.

assumptions: Score worst-case time and space. Pivot selection, comparisons, and list operations are O(1) per element. Expected-case notes assume uniformly random pivot ranks and distinct values. Exclude the input and final returned output; count retained partition lists and intermediate returned lists while recursive calls are active.
expected_auxiliary_space_exact: O(n^2) worst case; expected O(n) for uniformly random pivot ranks
expected_time_exact: O(n^2) worst case; expected O(n log n) with uniformly random pivot ranks and distinct values
rationale: Each call scans and partitions its k-element input in O(k), so maximally unbalanced pivots yield O(n²) worst-case time; random pivot ranks give expected O(n log n) time for distinct values. Active frames retain lesser/equal/greater partition lists totaling O(k) elements per frame. Their sizes sum to O(n²) for a maximally unbalanced chain, while random balanced partitions have O(n) expected peak retained list storage. Exclude the input and final returned list; intermediate partition/return lists remain auxiliary.

assumptions: Analyze a valid V×V adjacency matrix with nonnegative weights, 0 meaning no edge, valid source, and O(1) primitive and heap-node comparisons. Let E be the nonzero matrix entries and n=V+E. Each settled vertex scans a full matrix row. Exclude the input matrix and returned distances array from auxiliary space. Include the O(V) output printing in runtime; it is dominated.
input_size: V = vertexCount; E = nonzero matrix entries; n = V + E.
rationale: Owner-reviewed time and auxiliary-space rationale: The exact runtime is O(V² + E log(E+1)): up to V processed vertices each scan a full matrix row, and up to E successful relaxations create heap entries with O(log(E+1)) push/pop cost. Printing adds O(V), dominated. With n=V+E the correct coarse time class is O(n²), tight for sparse connected graphs; O(n log n) would miss the V² scan cost. The returned distances array is output; processed flags use O(V) and lazy duplicate heap entries use O(E), so auxiliary space is O(V+E), coarse O(n).

assumptions: Analyze minimumCoins, not change. Amount A≥1 and denominations are positive; C≥1. Use n=max(A,C) for coarse scoring and treat fixed-width integer operations as O(1). Exclude input and scalar output.
input_size: A = amount; C = number of coin denominations; n = max(A,C).
rationale: Time: The method initializes A+1 entries, then for each of A positive amounts scans all C coin denominations. Time is O(A*C + A); for A,C≤n this is O(n²). Auxiliary space: The single minimumCoins array has A+1 integer entries, so auxiliary space is O(A), bounded by O(n). Owner review: The DP array initialization costs O(A); the nested amount/coin loops cost O(A·C), so time is O(A·C). The single A+1-entry array gives O(A) auxiliary space. Under n=max(A,C), the coarse classes O(n²) time and O(n) space are valid. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial in numeric amount A.

assumptions: Analyze the iterative linear_search entrypoint only, not the recursive helper or command-line code. Element equality is O(1); input sequence is excluded.
rationale: Time: The loop compares items in order and may inspect every element when the target is absent or last. Each iteration does constant work.
